correctness.rationale: On the affine quotient the second derivative is precisely the hinge-mixture measure, so the unit total-variation ball gives the supremum of the L² kernel norms, attained by an interior atom. Equality in the Hilbert norm of the signed mixture forces a common normalized direction almost everywhere; distinct kernels cannot be proportional since their distributional second derivatives have atoms at different interior knots. The moving-knot CLT uses bounded second moments for the hinge expectation and an integrable square majorant of order min(1,|s|⁻²) after rescaling. For t→0 the three-interval bound is O(n⁻²)+O(t^(3/2)n^(-3/2)); reflection gives the bound at 1. Integration by parts for the Gaussian square profile gives 2(1−1/√2)/(3√π); the boundary-layer Jacobian and squared amplitude supply [t(1−t)]^(3/2). Its unique maximum is 1/8 at 1/2, proving both the sharp coefficient and localization of every maximizing sequence. An independent exact degree-two check gives 37/7290 at t=1/3 versus 1/320 at t=1/2, consistent with the stated finite-degree limitation.
residual_risks: The bounded computation is not a test of the infinite-degree limit or of finite-degree knot uniqueness; the limit is established analytically and uniqueness at each degree is not asserted.

value.rationale: For the natural curvature-variation ball this replaces a pointwise estimate by the sharp global approximation error, identifies all worst inputs, and finds the leading constant and every asymptotically worst knot. The distinction from ordinary BV and the failure of exact finite-degree centering make the localization more than a symmetry argument.
residual_risks: No claim is made for other Lp objectives or Bernstein variants.
